author: Sunshine Sentinel
title: Florida State women's golf draws No. 4 seed for Tallahassee regional - Sunshine Sentinel
text:
The Florida State women’s golf team announced on Apr. 29 that it will compete as the No. 4 seed in the upcoming NCAA Regional Championship, which will take place at Seminole Legacy from May 11 to May 13.
The event is significant as it marks the third time in program history that an NCAA Regional will be hosted in Tallahassee, and the first time at Seminole Legacy. The top five teams from this regional will advance to the NCAA Women’s Golf Championship, scheduled for May 22-27 at Omni La Costa Resort and Spa in Carlsbad, California.
According to the announcement, Florida State previously hosted regionals at Southwood Golf Club in 2014 and Don Veller Golf Course in 2018; Don Veller was renamed Seminole Legacy following a redesign completed on March 10, 2020. The team has had a successful season with victories during the 2025-26 campaign and six top-five finishes.
Sophia Fullbrook leads Florida State this season after securing back-to-back wins and earning ACC Co-Golfer of the Month honors for March. Fullbrook currently ranks No. 54 in the World Amateur Golf Rankings and No. 25 according to Scoreboard ranking.
Haruhi Nakatani also contributed significantly by leading all players with eighteen birdies during stroke play at the ACC Championship and finishing tied for sixth place—the highest finish by a freshman from Florida State since Frida Kinhult’s fifth-place tie at the tournament in 2019.
The field for this year’s Tallahassee Regional includes teams such as Florida (No.4), Wake Forest (No.9), UCLA (No.14), Kentucky, Purdue, Clemson, ULM, North Florida, Little Rock, Texas Rio Grande Valley, RV Eastern Michigan along with host school Florida State.
